notes: Stop names are the stop engraving. Each stop has three Voice Palette alternatives and the Organ Type piston switches between American Eclectic, English Cathedral, French Romantic and German Baroque voices.

The two Library/MIDI tabs of each division are engraved with a default library voice (Great: Contre Trompette 16, Grand Mixtur VIII; Swell: Clarion 4, Lieblich Gedackt 16; Pedal: Pedal Grand Mixture VI, Contre Bombarde 32) and are included under those names; they can be re-assigned to other library voices or to external MIDI.
Grand Mixtur VIII / Pedal Grand Mixture VI: footage not published, 2' entered as a placeholder.
MIDI channels are taken from the Inspire 234/240 owner's manual (same Rodgers/Roland platform generation); the Classic owner's manual was not found online - check on your organ.
MIDI channels: the keyboards always transmit on fixed channels Great 12, Swell 13, Pedal 14, whether or not a Library/MIDI coupler is on. Check on your organ.

Individual stop messages are not published. Pistons send either a Rodgers "STOP MAP" System Exclusive dump or a memory Program Change (set in the MIDI menu). Neither can be mapped to single stops, so every stop is unbound: use Learn every stop. If a stop sends nothing when you move it, it cannot be learned.
The controller sent by the expression shoes is not documented, so no expression mapping is set.

Stop list: https://www.rodgersinstruments.com/uploads/brochures/Rodgers_Classic_brochure.pdf (Rodgers Classic Series brochure, "Stoplist Classic Series 569", stop engraving column, PDF p. 8; same stops as the 559, adds toe pistons and divided expression)

MIDI scheme: https://www.rodgersinstruments.com/uploads/downloads/INSPIRE%20234%20240%20OM%5B30%5D.pdf (Rodgers Inspire 234/240 owner's manual, "About MIDI transmit channels", PDF p. 32: Great CH12, Swell CH13, Pedal CH14, fixed)
